```{=html}
<section class="u4h-hero" aria-labelledby="u4h-title">
  <p class="u4h-kicker">Unit 4 · Climate Change</p>
  <h1 class="u4h-title" id="u4h-title">Earth's air has more CO₂ than at any time in <span>800,000 years.</span></h1>
  <p class="u4h-lede">Since 1958, scientists on top of Mauna Loa in Hawaii have measured <b>carbon dioxide (CO₂)</b> in the air every month. Press play and watch it climb. Then <b>zoom out</b> to air bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice to see how unusual today really is.</p>
  <div class="u4h-dq"><strong>Unit driving question</strong>How do natural factors contribute to changes in Earth's temperature? What are 99.9% of climate scientists seeing in historical climate data that makes them so sure humans are the cause of climate change today, and why does it matter?</div>
```

```{ojs}
//| output: true
u4hViz = {
  // NOAA GML Mauna Loa monthly mean CO2 (ppm), March 1958 – September 2026, one value per month.
  const mlo = U4H_MLO;
  // Antarctic ice-core composite CO2 (Bereiter et al. 2015, NOAA NCEI), averaged into 1,000-year bins:
  // flat pairs [thousands of years before 1950, ppm], oldest first. Industrial-era samples (< 200 yr BP) left out.
  const iceFlat = U4H_ICE;

  const monthNames = ["January","February","March","April","May","June","July","August","September","October","November","December"];
  const modern = mlo.map((v, i) => {
    const m = 2 + i; // index 0 = March 1958
    const year = 1958 + Math.floor(m / 12), month = m % 12;
    return {t: year + (month + 0.5) / 12, v, label: `${monthNames[month]} ${year}`};
  });
  // Yearly means of full years, for the 800,000-year view
  const byYear = d3.rollups(modern, a => ({n: a.length, v: d3.mean(a, d => d.v)}), d => Math.floor(d.t));
  const yearly = byYear.filter(([, o]) => o.n === 12).map(([y, o]) => ({y, v: o.v}));
  const ice = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < iceFlat.length; i += 2) ice.push({ago: iceFlat[i] * 1000 + 76, v: iceFlat[i + 1], kind: "ice"});
  const NOW = 2026;
  const deep = ice.concat(yearly.map(d => ({ago: NOW - d.y, v: d.v, kind: "mlo", y: d.y})));
  const iceMax = d3.max(ice, d => d.v);

  const W = Math.round(Math.max(300, Math.min(720, width - 28))), H = W < 500 ? 270 : 330;
  const small = W < 500;
  const M = {top: 28, right: 14, bottom: 34, left: 42};
  const reduceMotion = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;

  const root = html`<div class="u4h-viz"></div>`;
  const tabs = html`<div class="u4h-tabs" role="group" aria-label="Choose a time span">
    <button class="u4h-tab" type="button" aria-pressed="true" data-mode="modern">Since 1958</button>
    <button class="u4h-tab" type="button" aria-pressed="false" data-mode="deep">🔭 Last 800,000 years</button></div>`;
  const read = html`<div class="u4h-read" aria-live="polite"><span class="u4h-ppm"></span><span class="u4h-when"></span></div>`;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).attr("role", "img");
  const controls = html`<div class="u4h-controls">
    <button class="u4h-play" type="button" aria-label="Play">▶</button>
    <input class="u4h-range" type="range" min="0" step="1" aria-label="Move through time"></div>`;
  const note = html`<p class="u4h-note"></p>`;
  root.append(tabs, read, svg.node(), controls, note);
  const playBtn = controls.querySelector(".u4h-play");
  const range = controls.querySelector(".u4h-range");
  const ppmEl = read.querySelector(".u4h-ppm"), whenEl = read.querySelector(".u4h-when");

  const gBand = svg.append("g"), gGrid = svg.append("g"), gX = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${H - M.bottom})`);
  const gY = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${M.left},0)`);
  const yLabel = svg.append("text").attr("x", 4).attr("y", 14).attr("fill", "#94a3b8").attr("font-size", 12).text("CO₂ (ppm)");
  const ghost = svg.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "rgba(148,163,184,0.25)").attr("stroke-width", 1.2);
  const lineIce = svg.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#7dd3fc").attr("stroke-width", 1.8).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
  const lineMain = svg.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
  const gNotes = svg.append("g");
  const dot = svg.append("circle").attr("r", 6).attr("fill", "#fde68a").attr("stroke", "#0b2530").attr("stroke-width", 2);

  const grad = svg.append("defs").append("linearGradient").attr("id", "u4h-grad").attr("x1", 0).attr("x2", 1).attr("y1", 0).attr("y2", 0);
  grad.append("stop").attr("offset", "0%").attr("stop-color", "#fbbf24");
  grad.append("stop").attr("offset", "100%").attr("stop-color", "#ef4444");

  const axisStyle = g => {
    g.selectAll("text").attr("fill", "#cbd5e1").attr("font-size", 13);
    g.selectAll("line,path").attr("stroke", "rgba(203,213,225,0.45)");
  };

  let mode = "modern", data = modern, idx = modern.length - 1, x, y;

  function setup() {
    data = mode === "modern" ? modern : deep;
    range.max = data.length - 1;
    gBand.selectAll("*").remove(); gNotes.selectAll("*").remove();
    if (mode === "modern") {
      x = d3.scaleLinear([1958, NOW + 1], [M.left, W - M.right]);
      y = d3.scaleLinear([305, 440], [H - M.bottom, M.top]);
      gX.call(d3.axisBottom(x).ticks(small ? 4 : 7).tickFormat(d3.format("d"))).call(axisStyle);
      lineMain.attr("stroke", "url(#u4h-grad)");
      lineIce.attr("d", null);
      ghost.attr("d", d3.line(d => x(d.t), d => y(d.v))(modern));
      svg.attr("aria-label", "Line graph of carbon dioxide measured at Mauna Loa, Hawaii, every month from 1958 to 2026. It rises from about 315 ppm to about 430 ppm, with a small up-and-down wiggle every year.");
    } else {
      x = d3.scaleLinear([806000, 0], [M.left, W - M.right]);
      y = d3.scaleLinear([160, 440], [H - M.bottom, M.top]);
      gX.call(d3.axisBottom(x).tickValues(small ? [800000, 400000, 0] : [800000, 600000, 400000, 200000, 0])
        .tickFormat(d => d === 0 ? "today" : `${d / 1000}k yrs ago`)).call(axisStyle)
        .call(g => g.selectAll(".tick:last-of-type text").attr("text-anchor", "end"));
      gBand.append("rect").attr("x", M.left).attr("width", W - M.left - M.right)
        .attr("y", y(300)).attr("height", y(170) - y(300)).attr("fill", "rgba(125,211,252,0.08)");
      gBand.append("line").attr("x1", M.left).attr("x2", W - M.right).attr("y1", y(300)).attr("y2", y(300))
        .attr("stroke", "#7dd3fc").attr("stroke-dasharray", "5 4").attr("stroke-opacity", 0.7);
      gNotes.append("text").attr("x", M.left + 8).attr("y", y(300) - 7).attr("fill", "#7dd3fc").attr("font-size", 13)
        .text("Highest natural level: about 300 ppm");
      lineMain.attr("stroke", "#ef4444");
      ghost.attr("d", d3.line(d => x(d.ago), d => y(d.v))(deep));
      svg.attr("aria-label", "Line graph of carbon dioxide over the last 800,000 years from Antarctic ice cores, then Mauna Loa. It swings between about 175 and 300 ppm in ice-age cycles, then shoots straight up to about 427 ppm in modern times.");
    }
    gGrid.selectAll("*").remove();
    gGrid.selectAll("line").data(y.ticks(5)).join("line")
      .attr("x1", M.left).attr("x2", W - M.right).attr("y1", d => y(d)).attr("y2", d => y(d))
      .attr("stroke", "rgba(203,213,225,0.12)");
    gY.call(d3.axisLeft(y).ticks(5).tickSize(0).tickPadding(6)).call(axisStyle).call(g => g.select(".domain").remove());
  }

  function show(i) {
    idx = Math.max(0, Math.min(data.length - 1, i));
    range.value = idx;
    const d = data[idx];
    if (mode === "modern") {
      lineMain.attr("d", d3.line(e => x(e.t), e => y(e.v))(modern.slice(0, idx + 1)));
      dot.attr("cx", x(d.t)).attr("cy", y(d.v));
      ppmEl.innerHTML = `${d.v.toFixed(1)}<small>ppm</small>`;
      whenEl.textContent = d.label;
      const rise = d.v - modern[0].v;
      note.innerHTML = idx === 0 ? "The very first month of measurements." :
        `That's <b>${rise > 0 ? "+" : ""}${rise.toFixed(1)} ppm</b> since March 1958. Notice the yearly wiggle: plants soak up CO₂ every Northern Hemisphere summer.`;
    } else {
      const iceSlice = data.slice(0, idx + 1).filter(e => e.kind === "ice");
      const mloSlice = data.slice(0, idx + 1).filter(e => e.kind === "mlo");
      lineIce.attr("d", d3.line(e => x(e.ago), e => y(e.v))(iceSlice));
      lineMain.attr("d", mloSlice.length ? d3.line(e => x(e.ago), e => y(e.v))([iceSlice[iceSlice.length - 1], ...mloSlice]) : null);
      dot.attr("cx", x(d.ago)).attr("cy", y(d.v));
      ppmEl.innerHTML = `${Math.round(d.v)}<small>ppm</small>`;
      if (d.kind === "ice") {
        whenEl.textContent = `about ${d3.format(",")(Math.round(d.ago / 1000) * 1000)} years ago`;
        note.innerHTML = d.v < 210 ? "🧊 A cold <b>ice age</b> (glacial period). Low CO₂, huge ice sheets."
          : d.v > 265 ? "🌿 A warm <b>interglacial</b> period, like the last 10,000 years."
          : "Air from a bubble trapped in Antarctic ice.";
      } else {
        whenEl.textContent = `${d.y} (Mauna Loa yearly average)`;
        note.innerHTML = `<b>${Math.round(d.v - iceMax)} ppm above</b> the highest point in the ice-core averages. Humans burning fossil fuels did this in about 150 years.`;
      }
    }
  }

  // Playback
  let timer = null, visible = false, played = false;
  const STEPS_PER_SEC = () => data.length / 6;
  function stop() { if (timer) { timer.stop(); timer = null; } playBtn.textContent = "▶"; playBtn.setAttribute("aria-label", "Play"); }
  function play() {
    if (reduceMotion) { show(data.length - 1); return; }
    if (idx >= data.length - 1) show(0);
    const start = idx;
    playBtn.textContent = "❚❚"; playBtn.setAttribute("aria-label", "Pause");
    timer = d3.timer(el => {
      const i = start + Math.floor(el / 1000 * STEPS_PER_SEC());
      show(i);
      if (i >= data.length - 1) stop();
    });
  }
  playBtn.addEventListener("click", () => timer ? stop() : play());
  range.addEventListener("input", () => { stop(); show(+range.value); });

  // Drag or tap on the chart to read values
  const node = svg.node();
  const nearest = e => {
    const b = node.getBoundingClientRect();
    const px = (e.clientX - b.left) * W / b.width;
    const key = mode === "modern" ? (d => d.t) : (d => -d.ago);
    const target = mode === "modern" ? x.invert(px) : -x.invert(px);
    return d3.leastIndex(data, d => Math.abs(key(d) - target));
  };
  node.addEventListener("pointerdown", e => { stop(); show(nearest(e)); });
  node.addEventListener("pointermove", e => { if (e.pointerType === "mouse" || e.buttons) show(nearest(e)); });

  tabs.addEventListener("click", e => {
    const b = e.target.closest(".u4h-tab"); if (!b || b.dataset.mode === mode) return;
    stop();
    mode = b.dataset.mode;
    tabs.querySelectorAll(".u4h-tab").forEach(t => t.setAttribute("aria-pressed", t === b ? "true" : "false"));
    setup();
    if (reduceMotion || !visible) show(data.length - 1); else { show(0); play(); }
  });

  setup();
  show(modern.length - 1);

  // Draw itself the first time it scrolls into view; pause when off screen
  const io = new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => {
    visible = entry.isIntersecting;
    if (!visible) stop();
    else if (!played && !reduceMotion) { played = true; show(0); play(); }
  }, {threshold: 0.35});
  io.observe(node);
  invalidation.then(() => { io.disconnect(); stop(); });

  return root;
}
```

## Anchor Phenomenon

> **Earth's temperature is rising, reversing the cooling trend that occurred over the past 2,000 years, putting millions of people in harm's way, yet the public is not convinced of the risks.**
>
> Climate has changed in the past because of natural factors. Today's change is different: 99.9% of climate scientists agree that **humans are the cause**, which also means humans can take action to limit the changes and their consequences.

## Unit Driving Question

> **How do natural factors contribute to changes in Earth's temperature? What are 99.9% of climate scientists seeing in historical climate data that makes them so sure humans are the cause of climate change today, and why does it matter?**

**Performance task:** *Educating your community about the predicted impacts of climate change on human populations.* You will communicate the scientific consensus to someone in your community who is skeptical. To do so, you will:

1. **Analyze and interpret data** to confirm that human activities are causing climate change right now
2. **Analyze and interpret data** to determine future impacts of climate change
3. **Explain** how these impacts are expected to affect human populations

## Unit Storyline

| Lesson | Question |
|---|---|
| [Unit Opening](unit4-opening.qmd) | How do natural factors contribute to changes in Earth's temperature, and why are scientists so sure humans are the cause today? |
| [Seasons (Optional)](unit4-seasons-optional.qmd) | How does the annual cycle of the Earth around the Sun create seasonal temperature variations? |
| [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd) | What factors have contributed to climate change in the past, and are they contributing to climate change now? |
| [Climate Feedbacks](unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd) | What is causing global temperatures to rise, and why is the Arctic warming at almost 4 times the rate of the rest of the globe? |
| [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd) | Have humans experienced dramatic climate change in the past? How were they impacted, and what does that tell us about the future? |
| [Unit Closing](unit4-closing.qmd) | What are scientists seeing in the data that makes them sure humans are the cause, and why does it matter to your community? |

## What You'll Figure Out

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

::: {.key-idea}
- ☀️ **Explain** how Earth's tilt and its orbit around the Sun cause seasonal temperature changes
- 🌀 **Use** orbital cycle data (eccentricity, tilt, and precession) to explain glacial and interglacial periods
- 📉 **Show** that orbital cycles and solar output point to slow cooling today, so they cannot explain current warming
- 🏭 **Explain** how carbon dioxide from human activities strengthens the greenhouse effect
- 🧊 **Model** how feedbacks like ice-albedo make the Arctic warm almost 4 times faster than the rest of the globe
- 🌊 **Describe** how past climate changes, like the end of the last ice age and the Younger Dryas, affected human populations
- 🏙️ **Predict** how future climate change will affect people, including your own community
:::
